requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Read the purchase information for every unit presented. PA-101 must be identified as Pocket P1 Pearl, Grade A, 64 GB, USD 99, with one USB-C cable and one zip case; PA-102 must be identified as Pocket P1 Graphite, Grade B, 64 GB, USD 79, with one USB-C cable and no zip case. The four fixed purchase labels must organize the corresponding information without swapping records. Each single-unit role must feature its designated unit; both-unit roles must present both. Front-led product cards show the front, and rear-led cards show the rear. Portrait panels identify their unit or units and their included accessories. Wording and layout may vary except for required verbatim text; missing information, mismatched associations or extra included accessories fail.

Each depicted handheld must retain its reference identity: Pearl #E8E5DE or Graphite #343A40 shell, rounded horizontal housing with the recorded proportions, centered landscape black screen, left cross-shaped directional pad, four right face buttons, two lower oval buttons, rear recess and corner screws, and centered top USB-C port with the power button to its left. PA-101 retains clear glass, matte buttons and port rim, and a 6 mm horizontal upper-right rear hairline. PA-102 retains clear glass, a 12 mm upper-right rear scratch descending rightward, the polished lower-right face button and the 3 mm pale scuff on the port's right lip. Judge locations in the relevant surface's viewing orientation. Changes in camera angle, crop and lighting are allowed, but visible surfaces must not be cleaned up, mirrored, recolored or assigned another unit's wear. Depicted included accessories must match the black USB-C-to-USB-C cable and charcoal fabric zip case identities.

Measure visible purchase lettering relative to each image's shorter edge. Unit identification, condition, included-item and price information must have text height of at least 2.5% of that edge and remain readable. Typeface and line arrangement may vary; undersized purchase text fails.

All four product cards place the handheld at 85–90% of canvas width in the white upper 75% product region, leave the 5% spacing band and put captions in the lower 20%. Each portrait reserves the lower 30% for text; all six landscape condition panels reserve the rightmost 30%. Front-led, rear-led and detail compositions may differ within their designated frames; incorrect scale or region placement fails.

The complete unit panels each contain front, rear, port, accessory and dimension views, with correct inventories and recorded wear. Their plain reference cards sit beside the handhelds at credible relative scale, with card dimensions 85 × 54 mm and handheld dimensions 160 × 76 × 18 mm. Dedicated rear panels clearly locate the Pearl's 6 mm horizontal upper-right hairline and Graphite's 12 mm descending diagonal upper-right scratch. Dedicated port-and-control panels show both the port and face buttons: Pearl remains matte, while Graphite exposes the polished lower-right button and 3 mm pale scuff on the port's right lip. Cropping and magnification may vary; omitted required views, misplaced wear or incorrect labels fail.

Each comparison contains two unit rows identifying PA-101 as Pocket P1 Pearl and PA-102 as Pocket P1 Graphite. The unit comparison covers grades, all recorded wear, 64 GB storage, USD 99 and USD 79, and accessory counts; its grade explanation links A to the light hairline and matte controls and B to the scratch, polished button and port scuff. The bundle comparison explicitly shows cable/case counts 1/1 and 1/0 and the corresponding complete bundle prices USD 99 and USD 79. Both retain the required purchase labels and matching records. Layout and explanation wording may vary; inconsistent prices, absent zero counts or ungrounded grade explanations fail.

All three boards compare PA-101 and PA-102 using their correct records. Across the boards, information priority, image treatment and the presentation of grade explanations must form three distinguishable approaches: condition-first, bundle-first and structured unit records. Different aesthetic solutions are allowed; recoloring an otherwise identical arrangement or omitting a unit does not constitute the requested comparison.

The note unambiguously selects one of the three supplied boards and states the continuing information order and arrangement. Its choice must be traceable to an actual board, with the alternatives established before the selection in the available process narrative. Any of the three may be chosen; an unnamed hybrid, multiple unresolved choices or no description of the retained arrangement fails.

The three sheets are each one page and follow the selected information arrangement. The hierarchy records selling points, priorities, placements and minimum text heights, explicitly including LOOP AGAIN, See the wear. Know the bundle. and 64 GB and respecting the 2.5% purchase-text minimum. The shot inventory gives each image's role, proportion and required content and assigns front, rear, port, control and bundle views to named final layouts. The variant table correctly records both units' IDs, full names, shell colors and codes, shared dimensions and storage, grades, all surface observations, accessory counts including Graphite's zero cases, and prices. Presentation may vary; incomplete records, wrong differences or missing view assignments fail.

The final images visibly implement the selected information priorities and the hierarchy sheet's placements, with recurring treatment of unit identity, grade, wear, included items and price. Adaptation to square, portrait, comparison and detail layouts is allowed; a final category that switches to an unrelated information arrangement or contradicts the selected hierarchy fails.

Every final image must visibly carry the hierarchy table's required store name, listing phrase and storage value: LOOP AGAIN, See the wear. Know the bundle. and 64 GB. Changes in placement and line wrapping are acceptable; omission or alteration on any final layout fails. Dedicated video and presentation checks cover the remaining media.

Review the complete video and timeline. It lasts ten seconds, allocating 0–5 seconds to PA-101 and 5–10 seconds to PA-102. Each segment visibly communicates the correct identity, grade, price, recorded wear and complete accessory inventory, with no swapped or extra items. Across the video, LOOP AGAIN, See the wear. Know the bundle. and 64 GB must be visibly repeated from the hierarchy. The selected information arrangement and reference shell colors, controls and visible marks must persist. Editing and camera treatment may vary; unequal unit allocations, reversed sequence, missing required facts or condition evidence, or contradictory product depictions fail.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation has at least ten pages and names the selected direction on page one consistently with the selection note. It develops that arrangement and includes LOOP AGAIN, See the wear. Know the bundle. and 64 GB. The fact-placement map accounts for the phrase, storage, both prices, the Pearl hairline, Graphite scratch, polished button, port scuff and both inventories, naming their final-layout destinations and corresponding video time ranges. Map format may vary; incomplete coverage, vague destinations, incorrect facts or conflicting direction choices fail. Actual reuse is assessed separately.

The presentation visibly reuses all three direction boards, the selection, all three planning sheets, every one of the fifteen final images and frames from the delivered video. Resizing and presentation-page arrangement are allowed; written sources may appear as readable reproductions or excerpts retaining their relevant content. Missing images, merely naming a source, illegible reproductions or substituting unrelated artwork fail.

Front-led and rear-led cards use the selected information arrangement and hierarchy, with unit-specific facts agreeing with the variant table. Changing the featured surface preserves each unit's shell identity, correct purchase record and visible recorded wear.

Complete panels and close-ups carry the selected information arrangement and agree with the planned view assignments and unit records. Rear, port and control details depict the same unit-specific wear as the corresponding complete panels, with correct accessory and dimension information.

Comparison and portrait panels retain the selected purchase-information arrangement used on the product cards, adapted to their different content and frames. Both-unit and individual-unit presentations agree on identities, grades, storage, prices, wear and included accessories, including Graphite's zero zip cases.
